title: Hybrid Model Orchestration for Secure Legal Analysis
business: A boutique law firm handling sensitive client contracts requiring strict data residency.
problem: The firm needs to analyze thousands of documents for clause extraction but cannot upload sensitive legal data to public cloud providers due to strict confidentiality agreements.
solution: The firm implements Ollama to run open-weight models locally on secure, air-gapped workstations for initial document processing, while using the Ollama API to route non-sensitive summary tasks to cloud-hosted models for advanced reasoning.
steps: Install the Ollama runtime on local secure workstations to host open-weight models.
Configure the local application to interface with the Ollama API for local document parsing.
Define a routing logic in the application layer to distinguish between sensitive data and general query tasks.
Integrate the Ollama API client to forward non-sensitive metadata to cloud-hosted models when necessary.
Verify that sensitive document text remains strictly within the local environment.
outcome: The firm achieves a balance between high-security local processing for sensitive data and the advanced reasoning capabilities of cloud models for general tasks, ensuring compliance with client privacy requirements.
limitation: The primary limitation is the hardware dependency for local models; if the local workstation lacks sufficient VRAM, inference speed will degrade significantly. Developers can check this by monitoring the local process memory usage and latency during model execution.
